findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this bucket are not covered by an enforced SSE-KMS or SSE-S3 default. The bucket holds a customer master data file, so stored PII is written without any configured encryption guarantee.

The resource is explicitly annotated '# bucket is public' and, unlike every other bucket here, specifies no acl and no accompanying aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block. With no block-public-access guard and no bucket-level policy, ACLs or policies can expose the customer master object to anonymous readers, and nothing in this configuration prevents it.

No bucket policy denies requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so this bucket accepts plain HTTP API calls. Credentials and the customer master data can therefore traverse the network unencrypted.

A customer master spreadsheet is uploaded with no kms_key_id and no server_side_encryption argument, into a bucket that itself defines no default encryption and is documented as public. Sensitive customer records are therefore stored unencrypted and potentially publicly reachable.

The object source points at resources/customer-master.xlsx, meaning the customer master data file is tracked in the Terraform repository alongside the code. Anyone with repository read access obtains the sensitive dataset without touching AWS.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is present, so financial records are stored without an enforced default encryption configuration, unlike the logs bucket which correctly uses a KMS CMK.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, leaving operational data stored without an enforced server-side encryption default.
The bucket configures versioning and access logging but omits server_side_encryption_configuration entirely, so data science datasets are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
